evidence: Direct explicit circuit construction; quantifies the power and limitation of sparsity alone. This is a baseline boundary lemma, not a resolution of the MCSP self-reducibility upgrade or the CJW transfer.
proved_step: For every n and every language slice L_n subseteq {0,1}^n with |L_n| <= S(n), there is a Boolean circuit C_n deciding L_n of size O(S(n)n). Proof: enumerate L_n as y_1,...,y_t, t<=S(n). For each y_i build the conjunction of n literals asserting x=y_i, using O(n) fan-in-2 gates; OR the t equality tests using O(t) gates. This circuit accepts exactly the listed strings, hence exactly L_n. For t=0 use the constant-zero circuit. Therefore if S(n) is polynomial, L is in P/poly by taking C_n as length-n advice-selected circuit; if S(n)=2^{n^beta}, this bound is exponential and does not imply P/poly.
